anomalies.observed: In the upper-middle block of sheet 1 the reset pull-up R3 (10K) has its top terminal on the +5V power symbol, but the tachometer pull-up R6 (10K) has its top terminal on the VCC power symbol; its bottom terminal carries the TACH label that also goes to U2 pin 3 (PB4) / U3 pin 3 (PB4). VCC is the unregulated input rail (J5 pin 2, U1 LM1117-5.0 VIN, C2, JP1, R1/Q1 source), while the ATtiny VCC pins (U2.8, U3.8) are on +5V, the LM1117 output.
anomalies.expected: Both MCU input pull-ups should return to the rail that powers the ATtiny, i.e. +5V. R6 (tach pull-up, an input to PB4) should be tied to +5V like R3 (reset pull-up), not to the raw VCC rail that feeds the regulator and the fan switch. With VCC being the fan/input supply (well above 5 V), a pull-up to VCC drives the tach input above the ATtiny's absolute maximum.

evidence.quote: R6 10K with its upper terminal on the VCC power symbol and its lower terminal on the TACH label (sheet 1, upper middle, next to R3 10K which sits on +5V)
U2 (ATtiny45-20P) pin 8 VCC / U3 (ATtiny13V-10S) pin 8 VCC tied to +5V; U1 (LM1117-5.0) VIN = VCC (pin 3), VOUT = +5V (pin 2)
the specification does not state a tach pull-up rail; standard practice is to pull an open-collector tach output up to the logic supply of the reading device

anomalies.impact: Whenever the fan's open-collector tach output is off, the TACH net (ATtiny PB4) is pulled to the unregulated VCC rail (typically the 12 V fan supply) instead of 5 V. The ATtiny's PB4 input then exceeds its absolute maximum (VCC+0.5 V) and its ESD clamp diode conducts continuously (~0.5 mA at 10K), which is outside the recommended injection-current limit and can corrupt tach readings or damage the MCU over time.

parsed.summary: The schematic is a sensible ATtiny fan controller (I2C/POT/TACH in, PWM out through R5 and the Q2/R1/Q1 high-side switch), but the tachometer pull-up R6 is returned to the raw VCC rail while the MCU and its other pull-up (R3) run from +5V, exposing the ATtiny tach input to the unregulated supply.
